entities/relationships.note: One row version per (subject_id, predicate, object_id, object_ref). valid_from is not part of the key, so a relationship that ends and later holds again (an ownership re-acquired) cannot be two rows yet.
entities/relationships.valid_from: Since registry-build-v2: for succeeded_by, the effective_date of the succession; for party_to, the agreement's effective_date; for located_within, and for controlled_by on basis statute (a body its enabling instrument makes a controlled body), the subject's valid_from. Blank for the rest, whose sources give no start: owned_by and controlled_by from Crown holdings, reports_to_minister (a lead department), member_of (ISC's association file has no dates; since registry-build-v3 a curated member row starts at its government's valid_from, which only the Tlicho Government has: 2005-08-04), governs, covers. Blank before registry-build-v2.
entities/relationships.valid_to: Since registry-build-v2, the subject's valid_to (no link outlives its subject), except succeeded_by, which never ends. Blank for a subject with none, and before registry-build-v2.

entities/mention_occurrences.note: One row version per occurrence_id. snapshot_id is the Iceberg snapshot the row was read from; spending_row_id is the spending table's id column; position is the index within an array field such as GAC recipients, else 0.
entities/mention_occurrences.province: Lowercase two-letter province code from the spending row, when it maps.
entities/mention_occurrences.city: The party's city as the spending row publishes it (recipient_city), trimmed. Blank when the source gives none, and on a research_org occurrence, since the row's city describes the recipient.
entities/mention_occurrences.postal_code: The party's postal code when it is a complete Canadian code, uppercase without spaces (A1A1A1). Blank when the source gives none, gives only the forward sortation area, gives a malformed value, or the party is outside Canada.
entities/mention_occurrences.fsa: The forward sortation area (A1A), the first three characters of postal_code, or a bare FSA as the source publishes it (proactive_contracts). Blank when the source gives neither.
entities/mention_occurrences.kind_reason: Why the party got its party_kind, as entities/occurrences.py decides it: grants_recipient_type_<code> (the grants recipient_type A, F, G, I, N, O, P or S), grants_researcher_name_type_<code> (since occurrences-v5: a recipient written as a researcher, "Surname, Given" or "Surname, Given-Institution", under an organization type, which is an individual; about 7,000 grants rows in release 7, over 99% of the 4,867 distinct names persons on review, the rest mostly type N "Name, Place" organizations), payer_field, institution_field, blank_name, blank_type_org_marker, blank_type_person_name_rule, blank_type_unsure_default_organization (since occurrences-v7: the person rule is unsure, so the party is an organization candidate; the spending data is public, and about 50 of 80 such names sampled in release 8 were organizations), blank_type_unsure_default_individual (the same case until occurrences-v6, excluded as an individual), withheld_name (since occurrences-v7: the name is only a withheld-name label such as REDACTED, Name withheld or Payment made to individual / Paiement émis à un individu, an individual whatever the recipient type), blank_type_roster_name (since occurrences-v6: the name equals, normalized, a current non-charity roster organization's name, such as Nunavut Tunngavik) and so on. Since occurrences-v7 a "Surname, Given" name in any case (SANDHU, MANJIT SINGH) is blank_type_person_name_rule. Since occurrences-v6 people named together need each side to be a person's name, so a trade or institution name joined by & is an organization; researcher names accept surname particles and lower-case names followed by an institution, and not foreign institution words or a legal form after the comma (Instituto Blacksmith México, A.C.). Since occurrences-v5 the person rule also marks an organization by a trade, community or Indigenous word (occurrences.TRADE_WORDS) unless the name also names a person ("Chad Parr Painting"), by a partnership or foreign legal form (GP, s.e.c., Sdn Bhd), or by an English and a French name joined by "|"; a title (Dr., Mr.) or a "Last, First (Affiliation)" name is an individual. On 8,286 blank-type excluded_individual rows sampled from release 7, 1,682 (1,022 names) became organizations, none of them a person's given name and surname; on 20,443 blank_type_org_marker rows, 121 became individuals, 119 of them researchers written "Last, First (University)". Entity creation reads the recipient type from it.
entities/mention_occurrences.country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the row places the party in (CA when a province maps and no country is given); blank where the source gives neither. For GAC recipients it is blank, since the field naming the recipient's country is unverified.
entities/mention_occurrences.create_unit: For an unlinked or created-member organization occurrence, its entity creation unit: its identifier (ca.cra.bn9:<bn9>, else org-id:<ref>), or name: followed by the JSON list [normalized name, province, place kind, place], place being the normalized city, else the FSA. Blank when the occurrence has neither an identifier nor a place, and for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.create_reason: For an unlinked no_candidate organization occurrence (or one fuzzy review left ai_undecided), why creation made no entity for its unit: too_few (fewer than three occurrences across two fiscal years or two sources, and no identifier; since create-v2 occurrences are counted as distinct evidence, so an archive-imported copy of a live row, the same spending row under <source>@archive_import, counts once, and so does a content copy of a row in one snapshot, a row with source_occurrence above 1 whose content equals an earlier row's), single_token, person_rule (a name the person rule calls an individual; since occurrences-v7 a name it is unsure of is not one), pending_review (fuzzy candidates awaiting AI review), identifier_held (another entity holds its identifier), identifier_conflict (names disagree under one identifier; queued), namesake_of_identified (its name and province belong to an identified unit; listed), namesake_unplaced (no city or FSA), roster_gap (government, academic or marker-word units, and since create-v4 units with a member whose name is a current roster entity's name, French name or alias, such as a federal body named in a recipient field; they go to fuzzy review and the roster gap list, never to creation) or rule_inactive (the unit passes the create rule but the create pair is not active: a proposal). Blank for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.row_date: The row's date under its source's date rule; see SOURCE_DATE_RULES in entities/occurrences.py.
entities/mention_occurrences.identifiers: Validated identifiers from the row as JSON, by namespace.
entities/mention_occurrences.roster_refs: For each candidate that is a roster reference (ca/ised/federal_corporations:<number>, a corporation with no entity yet, or first linked in this release), the roster row the release read, as JSON: {ref: {source_key, record_key, capture_id, row_sha256}}. row_sha256 is the digest of that row's record (rosters.row_sha256). Blank when no candidate is a roster reference.
entities/mention_occurrences.row_context: For an occurrence the rules left conflict or ambiguous, what AI review is shown from the spending row, as JSON: payer, program and description, each where the source publishes it (published columns payer, program, description). Never the amount. Blank for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.review_unit_id: For an occurrence the rules left conflict or ambiguous, its AI review unit key: the SHA-256 of everything the reviewer is shown (source, field, raw name, identifiers, province, city, postal code or FSA, period key, row_context, and each candidate with its pinned version: an entity's row_id in the release, or a roster reference's pin). Occurrences with the same key share one review. The period key is the fiscal year, or the row date where a candidate's validity changes inside that year. Also set for a no_candidate organization occurrence that has fuzzy_candidates, whose unit holds those candidates marked fuzzy and is reviewed under the fuzzy-v1 pair. Blank for every other occurrence.
entities/mention_occurrences.fuzzy_candidates: For a no_candidate organization occurrence whose normalized name has a municipal, university, hospital or First Nation marker word (goldset.MARKER_WORDS), its fuzzy-v1 candidates as a JSON list of refs, best first, at most 8: records sharing the name's rarest token in the release's token index, ranked by token overlap (Jaccard). A charity or First Nation is named by its entity ID; a federal corporation by its roster reference, pinned in roster_refs. Shown to AI review only, under the pair with candidate_generator fuzzy-v1; no rule links on them. Blank for every other occurrence.

entities/mentions.note: Rebuilt for every release. One row per (release_id, source_key, field, raw_name) with occurrences (count), linked (count linked; proposals are not links) and entity_ids (distinct entities linked).

entities/resolution_decisions.note: One row per decision, versioned like the other registry tables (row_id, content_sha256, source, recorded_at, release_id, retired_release_id). A decision is in force in the releases between release_id and retired_release_id; a replacement names it in supersedes, and no decision is edited. Columns decision_id, subject, subject_kind, outcome, entity_id, entity_ref, decider, versions, input_sha256, evidence, supersedes and retired_reason. AI review decisions are written by the release build from stored answers (fact-factory entities ai-review), one per occurrence of a review unit. Creation writes one created_member decision (decider rule, versions the create pair, input_sha256 the digest of the occurrence's create_unit, evidence unit_key and founding) per occurrence that joins a created entity; entity-level decisions (subject_kind entity, subject a created entity) are redirect (entity_id the survivor; by a reviewer, or by the redirect pair once active), correction (a reviewer keeping the entity, which reverses a redirect) and same_as (entity_ref.ref a roster record that covers the entity and attaches to its ID). A decision can have several row versions (overridden_by is added in a new one); decision_id stays.
entities/resolution_decisions.source: The decider as origin, such as {"origin": "ai"}.

publication/api_read_model.note: The `api` schema (src/fact_factory/serve/api_schema.sql): the allowlisted read model the public API reads, built after each registry release (docs/RUNBOOK.md, "API read model"). Every table and column is listed in src/fact_factory/serve/allowlist.py, and the blocking check api_columns_allowlisted fails the build if the live schema differs. Versioned tables use release_from and release_to; unchanged rows are not copied. No table holds a street address, raw_json, raw_xml or extra_json, and no full postal code for anyone but an organization recipient: spending parties carry fsa only, and spending_records.recipient_postal_code is the FSA unless the row's recipient is an organization (york_factory DECISIONS.md 20). Entity attributes carry no address keys (DECISIONS.md 19). Columns keep the shared definitions of their warehouse or spending columns unless stated below.
publication/api_read_model.releases: One row per registry release the model serves; the row is written last in its build transaction, so a reader that sees release_id N sees all of it. Columns release_id (the registry release), published_at (when the registry release was published), built_at (when the read model finished building it), code_revision (the commit that built the registry release), build_version (the registry build version), roster_captures (the roster captures the release pinned, from registry_releases.inputs), spending_snapshots (per occurrence source label, such as sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants or sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants@archive_import: snapshot_id, rows, duplicates (repeated record keys left out), changed and the rows added and closed), snapshot_basis (recorded when the release recorded its pinned snapshots, derived when they were read from its occurrences, for releases before the read model), counts (rows added and closed per table, previous_release), checks (the registry checks as name, passed and blocking, and the read model checks with their metadata) and build_seconds.
publication/api_read_model.entities: warehouse.entities, allowlisted columns. attributes has every object key matching address or street removed at any depth: a school board's addresses, and any other address attribute, are not served in v1 (york_factory DECISIONS.md 19); api_no_address_keys checks it. name_fr and redirected_to as in entities/entities.
publication/api_read_model.entity_names: One row per name, French name or alias of an entity version: kind (name, name_fr or alias), name as published, normalized_name (names.normalize), match_key (names.match_key, the exact-name search key) and normalization (the names version, such as names-v2), with the entity version's row_id, entity_id, release_from and release_to.
publication/api_read_model.relationships: warehouse.entity_relationships, allowlisted columns; attributes without address keys, as for entities.
publication/api_read_model.spending_parties: warehouse.mention_occurrences, one row version per occurrence. asset_key and acquisition split the occurrence source_key label (sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants@archive_import is asset_key sources/ca/tbs/proactive_grants, acquisition archive_import). spending_row_id is the spending table's id: join api.spending_records on (asset_key, acquisition, id), which can match one record per resource that holds the row. position, kind_reason, city, fsa, country, row_date, identifiers, create_reason as in entities/mention_occurrences. An individual's raw_name and normalized_name are published as the source wrote them (decided 2026-09-28); its place is city, province and fsa only, never a full postal code (api_individual_addresses_coarse). Left out: postal_code, roster_refs, row_context, review_unit_id, fuzzy_candidates and create_unit.
publication/api_read_model.spending_records: One version of one spending source row of the Iceberg snapshot the release pinned, per slice (asset_key and acquisition), from its typed columns: every column of the spending tables but raw_json, raw_xml and extra_json; revision_rank and commitments_json are JSON. recipient_postal_code is the code as published only when the row's recipient is an organization in the release (a recipient or vendor_name party of party_kind organization, and none of another kind); otherwise, for an individual and for a row with no organization recipient party, it is the forward sortation area, the first 3 characters without spaces, uppercased (york_factory DECISIONS.md 20). A record loaded whole whose recipient a later release reads as an individual gets a new version with the FSA in that release (counts.spending_records.postal_codes_reduced); api_individual_postal_codes_fsa blocks otherwise. The key is spending_key. A slice whose pinned snapshot is the previous release's is not read again; otherwise its rows are diffed by spending_key and a content hash of these columns, so an unchanged row keeps its version. A spending_key the snapshot repeats keeps its first row, and the count is in releases.spending_snapshots.
publication/api_read_model.spending_summary: One row per (release_id, entity_id, role, asset_key, fiscal_year, currency) under fixed rules: only linked (entity_id set) live occurrences, never archive_import; one row per source, never summed across sources; role payer, recipient (recipient, recipients and vendor_name fields) or research_org; a live record held in several resources counts once; where the table ranks revisions (revision_rank), only the highest-ranked revision per canonical_id counts. record_count, agreement_count, amount (sum of the counted amounts in currency; blank when none has an amount, never 0 for missing), amount_missing_count, aggregated_excluded (is_aggregated rows left out), revisions_excluded (lower revisions left out). measure names what amount measures: contract_value (proactive contracts), aggregated_contract_value, agreement_value (grants: not money paid), payments_or_expenditure (transfer payments), award_amount (NSERC, SSHRC, CIHR) or commitment (GAC). source_key is the adapter.
publication/api_read_model.release_exports: One row per bulk file of an exported release: table_name (the api table, or manifest.json), object_key (releases/<release_id>/<table>.parquet), url (the public URL when the export was written), sha256, rows (blank for the manifest), bytes, created_at.

publication/release_exports.note: Bulk files of each release the read model serves (src/fact_factory/serve/exports.py; docs/RUNBOOK.md, "Release exports"): releases/<N>/entities.parquet, identifiers.parquet, relationships.parquet and spending_parties.parquet, and releases/<N>/manifest.json, on the public bucket (files.buildcanada.com once its custom domain is live). Each file is one api table as of release N (api.in_release), ordered by row_id, zstd-compressed, with the same columns and definitions as that table except release_to, which a later release would change. JSON columns (aliases, attributes, source, identifiers, candidates) are JSON text. Keys are immutable. The manifest gives each file's path (relative to the manifest), sha256, rows, bytes and columns, the release's pinned inputs and the dictionary's sha256. export_counts_match_api and export_columns_allowlisted block before anything is uploaded.

publication/public_catalog.note: catalog/latest.json points at the current index.json (content-addressed). Since 2026-09-29 a run whose index content (everything but generated_at) equals the latest one's publishes nothing, and each published index is appended to warehouse.catalog_history and catalog/history.json (entries index_sha256, url, visible_from in Unix seconds and visible_from_utc; the catalog current at a time T is the last entry with visible_from <= T; before the first entry nothing was recorded). The index adds releases (per exported registry release: release, manifest and tables, each with key, url, sha256, bytes and, for tables, rows), history (its URL and rule) and dictionary (catalog/dictionary.json, the machine-readable export of this file, and its sha256; also listed under exports as dictionary.json).
